unit: from the waterway for shade structures, screen enclosures and tall planters; decks per height
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale measures every waterway yard from the wet face of the seawall. A deck at or below the ground-floor level needs no setback at all, a raised deck must stay 5 ft from property lines and no more than 2.5 ft above the finished floor, and gazebos, tiki huts, trellises and pool screen enclosures must stay 10 ft back from the water.
detail_rows: Where the yard is measured :: A yard along a waterway is measured from the face of the seawall in contact with the water (the wet face), or from the edge of the waterway where there is no seawall. ULDR Sec. 47-2.2.S. | At-grade decks :: Allowed in front, rear and side yards with no required setback, but not higher than the finished floor elevation of the ground floor. ULDR Sec. 47-19.2.G.1. | Above-grade decks :: Allowed in required yards no closer than 5 ft to any property line and no more than 2.5 ft above the ground-floor finished floor elevation; a visible vertical edge must be finished to match the deck. Sec. 47-19.2.G.2. | Gazebos, tiki huts, trellises :: In the rear yard, 10 ft from the waterway; open on all sides, max 12 ft tall, max 200 sq ft in the yard, one per plot. Sec. 47-19.2.P. | Pools and screen enclosures :: Single-family pools 5 ft from any property line and not above the ground-floor finished floor; setback measured from the outer edge of coping. Screen enclosures 10 ft from a property line abutting a waterway, max 12 ft tall in the rear yard, and no more than 5% of required pervious area may sit inside them. Sec. 47-19.2.BB. | Planters :: On a waterway, planters taller than 2.5 ft above grade stay 10 ft from the waterway. Sec. 47-19.2. | Sheds and tanks :: Utility sheds on a waterway lot must meet the district yard for that side (otherwise 5 ft from lines), max 10 ft tall, 12 ft per side and 100 sq ft, one per development site; satellite dishes stay 10 ft from the property line abutting the waterway. Sec. 47-19.2 (EE, satellite dish antennas). | Where it lives :: Unified Land Development Regulations Sec. 47-19.2 'Accessory buildings, structures and equipment, general' and Sec. 47-2.2 'Measurements'. | Guards (state rule) :: Florida Building Code, Residential, 8th Edition (2023), Sec. No local guard amendment was found in this city's code.

detail_rows: Shoreline setback :: The City requires minimum coastal setbacks of 10 to 20 ft from the mean high tide line of man-made water bodies and/or lawfully altered shorelines of natural water bodies, dependent on the particular shoreline characteristic. Code Sec. 122-1145(b)(1). | Raised platforms after a flood retrofit :: Elevated platforms for mechanical equipment may sit 5 ft from rear and side lines when a home is raised, but they are limited to non-habitable space and may not include elevated decks or patios. Sec. 122-1145(b)(1)g.2. | Pools :: In-ground pools 5 ft from all property lines. A pool or spa extending more than 30 inches above existing ground is a structure: 5 ft side and rear plus 5 ft from the house. Pools need a fence or wall at least 4 ft high. Sec. 122-1185. | Seawalls :: Shoreline hardening is allowed only where erosion critically imperils upland property and vegetation has failed; riprap is the first alternative and new hardening should generally not be vertical seawalls or bulkheads. unit: minimum buffer from MHW or mangrove roots for accessory structures on canal lots
qualifier: Marathon's water-resource buffer table puts houses 20 ft from mean high water on canal lots (10 ft on lots under 4,500 sq ft) and accessory structures, including non-enclosed decks, gazebos and pools, at least 10 ft back. On unaltered shorelines accessory structures need 25 ft.
detail_rows: Buffer table :: Principal structure on manmade canals, channels, basins and lawfully altered shorelines 20 ft; small lots under 4,500 sq ft 10 ft; open water unaltered 50 ft; measured from the MHWL or the landward extent of the mangrove root system, whichever is further landward. LDR Sec. 106.28, Table 106.28.1. | Accessory structures :: 10 ft minimum on canals and altered shorelines, 15 ft on filled open-water shorelines, 25 ft on unaltered shorelines; footnote lists outdoor recreational accessory structures such as non-enclosed decks, gazebos, pools, spas, permanent barbecues and fish cleaning tables. Docks, pilings, fences, ramps, seawalls and walkways are excepted. Table 106.28.1. | Buffer protection :: The buffer keeps existing undisturbed vegetation; wetlands may not be filled to meet the buffer; unpermitted alteration requires restoration at a 3:1 ratio. Sec. 106.28. | Wetland buffers :: Wetlands without listed species need a 50 ft buffer, reducible to an average of 25 ft (never under 15 ft) if the whole setback is planted in native vegetation with a stormwater plan, a conservation easement and a solid wall or fence at least 6 ft tall. Table 106.28.1. | Guards (state rule) :: Florida Building Code, Residential, 8th Edition (2023), Sec. R312.1.1-R312.1.3: a guard is required on open sides of a walking surface located more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below at any point within 24 inches of the open edge; it must be at least 36 inches high; openings must not let a 4-inch sphere pass. No local guard amendment was found in this city's code.
